Import first, add location second

How to transfer digital camera photos to iPhone.

Connect the camera or an SD card reader, open Apple Photos, choose Import, and select the photos you want. If your camera did not record GPS, importing will not create a location—but you can add one after the photos are safely in your library.

Published and reviewed September 17, 2026

How are the photos getting to the iPhone?

Camera connection

Connect a supported camera or adapter, open Photos, choose Import, then select the photos you want.

  • Photo imported✓
  • Capture time preserved✓
  • GPS location presentNot recorded

Apple Photos import

Transfer from a camera or SD card.

  1. Connect the deviceUse a compatible adapter, cable, or SD card reader for your iPhone or iPad. Power requirements vary by camera and accessory.
  2. Open Photos and choose ImportThe Import view appears when iOS recognizes the connected camera or storage device.
  3. Select and importChoose specific items or import all. Wait for the transfer to finish before disconnecting the camera, card, or adapter.
  4. Verify the photos in the libraryOpen several originals, inspect their capture dates, and confirm the expected images arrived.
Need device-specific details?

Apple maintains the current connection and import steps in its iPhone User Guide.

Why the Photos map may still be empty

Your photos made it to the iPhone. Their locations may not have.

Importing copies the photo and the metadata already inside it. It preserves GPS when GPS exists; it cannot create coordinates that the camera never recorded.

✓

GPS was in the file

Apple Photos can display the existing location after import. Open Info and look for a map or place name.

—

The camera had no GPS

The image may retain capture time, camera model, lens, and exposure while the location field remains empty.

⌁

You have other timeline evidence

A GPX track or geotagged iPhone photos from the same trip can provide location clues after import.

Diagnose before adding anything

Check whether the photo already has a location.

  1. Open a camera photo in PhotosUse an original from the imported batch, not a screenshot or a social-media copy.
  2. Swipe up or tap InfoIf a map and place name appear, Apple Photos already has a library location for that item.
  3. Compare several photosOne image may contain GPS while another does not, especially if location recording was intermittent or files came through different workflows.

If you know the place, use the built-in adjustment steps →

When a whole trip is missing

Use time to suggest a different place for each photo.

LensPin does not transfer photos from the camera. It begins after import, scans camera photos that lack locations, and matches their capture times against a GPX track or nearby iPhone photos.

Import questions

Camera photos on iPhone

Does LensPin transfer photos from a camera?

No. Use Apple Photos, a card reader, or the camera maker's official workflow. LensPin works after the photos are in Apple Photos.

Why did the capture date transfer but not the location?

Capture time and GPS are separate metadata fields. Most cameras record time; many do not have a GPS receiver or did not have location recording active.

Can I use camera Wi-Fi instead of a card reader?

You can use any workflow that places the original-quality photo in Apple Photos with its camera and capture-time metadata intact. Check a sample file before importing a large batch.

What if the imported photo is only in iCloud?

LensPin may need to download the asset to inspect original metadata or create an optional EXIF edit. See iCloud Photos support.
